paraphrase: In the assembly just after the awakening, the Buddha is seen as Vairocana whose body fills the dharmadhātu; worlds as numerous as atoms appear in each pore and in each atom; bodhisattvas and gods praise him.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase.

paraphrase: Pure practice (jingxing): the bodhisattva turns every daily act into a vow for beings — on waking, dressing, washing, eating, walking, seeing trees or water, he wishes that all beings may attain the corresponding good (some 140 such vows).
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase.

paraphrase: At the time of the first arousal of the mind (of awakening) one attains unsurpassed perfect awakening, knowing that all dharmas are the mind's own nature and becoming the wisdom-body without depending on another's awakening.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase. Chapter location from memory; the sentence 初發心時便成正覺 is a Huayan watchword.

location.section: 80-fasc. ch. 20 (夜摩宮中偈讚品), juan 19; 60-fasc. ch. 16

paraphrase: Verse of the bodhisattva Juelin: the mind is like a skilled painter who paints all the aggregates; there is nothing in all the worlds not made by it; mind, buddha and beings — these three are without difference; whoever wishes to know all buddhas of the three times should contemplate the nature of the dharmadhātu: all is made by mind alone.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase. The last quatrain (若人欲了知三世一切佛，應觀法界性，一切唯心造) is in the 80-fascicle version; the 60-fascicle version reads differently for that line.

location.section: 80-fasc. ch. 37 (如來出現品); 60-fasc. ch. 32 (寶王如來性起品) — the Tathāgatotpattisaṃbhavanirdeśa

paraphrase: The Tathāgata's wisdom is present in full in the bodies of all beings, but beings, deluded and clinging, do not know it — like a great sūtra-scroll recording the whole trichiliocosm contained within a single atom, which a wise man breaks open to benefit all; the Buddha teaches them the noble path to remove false thinking.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase.

paraphrase: The Lotus-Treasury world-ocean (Kusumatalagarbhavyūhālaṃkāra), purified by Vairocana's vows, in which innumerable world-systems rest on a great lotus in a sea of fragrant water, our Sahā world among them.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase.
